<reflection>
Adding product only improved fits uniformly across most mechanisms - discrimination is still weak. M4 and M5 remain clearly worse. M17 is slightly best but all top 18 mechanisms are within ~0.5 NLL units. The data isn't revealing mechanism-specific features at these conditions. I need conditions that amplify the unique features of specific mechanisms.

Key discriminators I haven't yet explored:
- Very low catalyst: amplifies deactivation effects (M9, M13, M18, M20) and catalyst dimer mechanisms (M2, M3)
- Very high substrate: stresses substrate inhibition (M7, M11, M16) 
- High catalyst: catalyst-dimer mechanisms (M2, M3, M13, M19) behave differently

I should probe catalyst order by using a very different catalyst concentration.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Running with high catalyst loading will differentiate mechanisms with catalyst-catalyst interactions (M2, M3, M13, M19) versus simple mechanisms. In M3 especially, rate depends on [cat2] (dimer) and hence ~[cat]^2 dependence. In M2, cat dimerization sequesters cat (rate decreases). M13, M19 have bimolecular cat deactivation. Also, high catalyst shortens timescale and reveals early-time kinetics. Combined with moderate substrate, we can look at TOF differences.

Choose cat=0.05 (5x higher), S=1.0, P=0.
</hypothesis>
